name: Startup SG Founder
confidence_note: Eligibility criteria are consistent across all sources checked. The grant quantum and matching ratio were found ONLY on vendor blogs — Enterprise Singapore's own scheme page could not be reached at the URL tried. Do not quote a dollar figure on stage without a primary source. See docs/SOURCES.md.
quantum_note: Reported as S$20,000 to S$50,000 on a 1:1 matching basis, revised from 3:1 effective 1 April 2024. UNVERIFIED against a primary source — attribute, do not assert.
_notes: This grant is the demo's not_a_fit case, and it earns that state honestly: two of its criteria are irreversible. A founder who has previously incorporated cannot become a first-time entrepreneur again. Surfacing that in ninety seconds instead of after three weeks of paperwork is precisely problem P1.
No criterion here depends on the grant quantum, so the unverified dollar figure cannot produce a wrong eligibility answer. It is display metadata only.

criteria.terminal_reason: Citizenship status is outside the scope of anything this product can advise on.
There is no action a founder can take to become a first-time entrepreneur again. Offering a remedy here would be a lie.

criteria.requirement: Must not have previously incorporated a business
criteria.terminal_reason: Past incorporation is a matter of ACRA record and cannot be undone.
criteria._rationale: Distinct from is_incorporated. A founder can be currently unincorporated yet have incorporated before — that history still disqualifies. Collapsing the two fields would silently pass ineligible founders.

criteria.requirement: Business concept must not have received other government funding
criteria.terminal_reason: Funding already received cannot be un-received. This is why the forward-looking warning on the YCM card matters.

criteria.requirement: Must hold, or propose to hold, at least 30% equity in the company
criteria.remedy: Restructure the proposed cap table so you hold at least 30%.

criteria.requirement: Requires a Letter of Recommendation from an Accredited Mentor Partner — applications do not go directly to Enterprise Singapore
criteria.remedy: Approach an Accredited Mentor Partner (17 in the first appointed batch, including NUS Enterprise, NTUitive, SMU IIE and ACE). The AMP screens for qualification, works with you to draw up a development plan with milestones, then recommends you to the agency.
criteria._rationale: B's schema models this as an enum rather than the boolean C originally proposed, and the enum is better: IN_DISCUSSION is a real and common state. A founder mid-conversation with an AMP is not in the same position as one who has not started, and the UI can say so.

criteria.requirement: Reported to require co-matching capital at a 1:1 ratio, with at least half already paid up in ACRA BizFile at the point of application
criteria.remedy: Plan for co-matching capital before approaching an AMP.
criteria._rationale: blocking is FALSE because the matching ratio comes only from vendor blogs. Blocking a founder on an unverified figure would be exactly the kind of confident wrong answer this product exists to prevent. It surfaces as advice carrying its own uncertainty.

warnings.message: The grant amount and matching ratio shown here come from published guides rather than Enterprise Singapore directly. Confirm current figures with an Accredited Mentor Partner before planning around them.
